Looping in needed context from Legal ops and procurement playbook — high level thoughts: 

- Term: we can accept a 12-month renewal cadence only if we keep a 24-month firm commitment for pricing protection (i.e., Helix pays for 24 months upfront or commits to 24 months at current rates, with an annual billing option). This preserves our ability to amortize onboarding credits.
- Indemnity: reciprocal indemnities are reasonable; propose a counter of mutual indemnity for IP and third-party claims, with a negligence clause limited to the greater of $250k or 6 months of fees. That reduces open risk while being acceptable to some enterprise buyers.
- SLA credits: 6x monthly fee is higher than our cap. Suggest 4x for critical incidents and include a carveout for repeat systemic failures where we agree a remediation plan instead of per-incident credit inflation.
- Audit logs: we can add quarterly exports for Helix but need a clear security-evidence request flow and proof-of-request SLA (48 hours to produce).

Quick internal decision: proceed with a two-part compromise we can present to Helix tomorrow. Draft language below for Section 4.2 (Term and Renewal):

"4.2 Term; Renewal. The initial Term shall be twenty-four (24) months. Thereafter, the Agreement shall renew automatically for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the then-current renewal date. Customer may elect annual billing; pricing in effect at the time of the initial Term shall be guaranteed for twenty-four (24) months from Effective Date, subject to the fees schedule set forth on the Order Form."

For indemnity (Section 7): use Ben's suggested cap but tighten definitions: carve out claims from misuse and wilful misconduct, retain mutual IP indemnity. I will attach an updated Order_Form_v4.xlsx that shows the 25% onboarding buffer as a line item and two billing options: 24-month pricing guarantee vs annual billing.

We should ask Helix to confirm acceptance of: (A) the above renewal mechanics; (B) a mutual indemnity with the financial cap Ben proposed; (C) a quarterly audit-export cadence with 48-hour production SLA. If they push on SLA credits (6x), propose 4x with a remediation plan addendum.

1) Term: we will accept a rolling 12-month renewal at the Helix request, provided we include a 24-month pricing guarantee (see attached Order_Form_v4.xlsx). This gets Helix the annual cadence you need for budgeting and preserves pricing protection for Redwood.

3) SLA credits: Redwood proposes 4x monthly service fee for critical incidents, with a remediation plan trigger for repeated failures.

4) Audit logs / retention: Redwood accepts 18 months retention and will provide quarterly export on request with a 48-hour production SLA; exceptions for exceptionally large exports (we'll coordinate sampling and scoping).
